evidence_quotes.quote: Prevalence and risk factors of intestinal protozoal infections among patients in Malaysia: A systematic review and meta-analysis
This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate prevalence, identify risk factors, and evaluate detection methods.

According to a meta-analysis of ten risk factors, the pooled prevalence of protozoal intestinal infections was significantly higher (between 38% and 52%) in children under 15 years of age, in males, in those with low income or no formal education, and in those exposed to untreated water, poor sanitation or unhygienic practises.

raw_response.plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both the narrow rule-type and plain/broad Criterion 2 readings because this is a clinical/epidemiological meta-analysis of intestinal protozoal infection prevalence and diagnostic detection methods with no legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, or governance exposure and no water/sanitation service-access outcome.
raw_response.rationale: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates the clinical/epidemiological prevalence, demographic/behavioural/environmental risk factors, and diagnostic detection methods for intestinal protozoan infections among patients in Malaysia. Although exposure to untreated water and poor sanitation is included among ten epidemiological risk factors for infection, the study does not examine household/community water or sanitation service access as its subject (failing C1, E01), evaluates no legal, administrative, regulatory, or institutional mechanism (failing C2), and measures parasitic infection prevalence rather than any water or sanitation access outcome (failing C4).
